exercise.name: Lever Seated Leg Curl

reference.title: Lever Seated Leg Curl
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Seated leg curl machine (lever on the knee axis, heel roller, thigh hold-down pad)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you curl, breathe in as the legs straighten.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short squeeze, about 2.3 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Stack load is user-chosen: curl fully without the hips sliding forward.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower lowering

cues.text: Sit with the back on the pad, knees lined up with the lever axis, the roller behind the lower calves and the thigh pad snug above the knees; hold the side handles.
Breathe out and curl the heels down and back under the seat.
Squeeze the hamstrings with the knees well bent.
Breathe in and let the legs straighten slowly.
Pause with the knees nearly straight without letting the stack rest.

mistakes.mistake: Knees not on the lever axis
mistakes.fix: Line the knee joints up with the pivot.
Lock the thigh pad down and hold the handles.
Curl until the knees are well bent.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to well bent (clinical opinion)
Lever pivot on the knee joint so the roller does not slide on the calf (clinical opinion)
Behind the lower calves above the heels (clinical opinion)
Seated with the hips flexed, which keeps the hamstrings long (clinical opinion)
Leg curls load the hamstrings well, especially the lateral and medial hamstrings in flexion (McAllister 2014)
About 1.2 s down and 2.3 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5073, Lever Seated Leg Curl, video (movement reference)
McAllister, Hammond, Schilling, Ferreria, Reed & Weiss 2014, muscle activation during various hamstring exercises (J Strength Cond Res 28(6):1573-1580)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Stack load is user-chosen: start light.
Cramping in the hamstrings: lighten the load and shorten the hold.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee discomfort: shorten the range at the bent end.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Prime mover: bends the knee against the roller (McAllister 2014 for hamstring exercise EMG).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Prime mover: bends the knee against the roller (McAllister 2014 for hamstring exercise EMG).
muscleNotes.calves_r: The gastrocnemius helps bend the knee.
muscleNotes.calves_l: The gastrocnemius helps bend the knee.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk on the pad.
